newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower as rally falters.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end lower as rally falters.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended lower on Wednesday as the market took a breather after recent strong gains, but dealers said the downside looked well supported.
The lead Nikkei 225 June contract shed 190 points to close at 20,060, 20 points above its intra-day low.
"The charts still show an uptrend, but maybe it's a bit overbought," a trader with a Japanese futures house said.
He said the June Nikkei could slip back below 20,000 but should be well bid around 19,800 for the time being.
Comments by various Japanese officials, which inspired choppy trading in the dollar/yen, left many dealers confused.

The trader at the Japanese house said the June Nikkei rebounded initially on the back of the dollar's surge when key Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara said it would be difficult to procure funds for forex intervention directly from the money market.
The dollar later came off when another Finance Ministry official said Japan could use its $220 billion in external reserves to intervene in forex markets if needed.

A comment by Bank of Japan governor Yasuo Matsushita that the central bank's prolonged easy monetary policy in the 1980s was one factor behind the "bubble" economy stoked fears of a rate rise -- another negative factor for the Nikkei.
Taiwan stock index futures ended near their highs as stocks rallied on news of a cabinet reshuffle.
The May MSCI Taiwan index contract settled at 349.7 against its opening 342.0 on volume of 1,265 lots.
Refco Singapore Pte Ltd partly attributed the gains to reports of strong demand for computer chip products in March, which boosted the semiconductor sub-sector of Taiwan's weighted share index.
